LESSON: ANGLES

Grade: SNE  /  visual-impairment / Grade four
Subject: MATHEMATICS
Strand: Geometry
Topic 3.2: Angles
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 5

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Angles, part of Geometry in SNE  /  visual-impairment / Grade four MATHEMATICS.

Key inquiry question: How can you identify angles from the objects? 2. How do you identify an angle at a point?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

Refer to the KICD curriculum reference at the end of this lesson for the full list of outcomes.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

Follow your teacher’s guidance for group work, discussion, and practice on this topic.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Angles together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
● Communication and collaboration: The learner develops speaking and listening skills when discussing and

recognizing angles that are made by 2 lines that meet at point.

● Learning to learn: The learner makes clockwise quarter and half turns, and relate the turns to angles.

Values:
● Responsibility: The learner explores angles from the objects such as cubes, cuboids in the environment.

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
(PCIs):

58

• Environmental education: The learner explores and identifies angles from the objects such as cubes, cuboids in

the environment.

Link to other subjects:

• Creative Arts: The learner is able to relate angles from objects such as cubes and cuboids in the environment to

perspective.

Suggested Learning Resources:

Clay, plasticine, paper cutouts, pair of scissors, tactile angles, models of angles, toys, geometrical shapes, models of different

angles and digital devices with assistive technology such as screen readers, adapted keyboards and screen magnifiers.
